note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in WA.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Cape Flattery Tribal Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 112 and Bayview Ave from the eastern Makah Reservation line through Neah Bay to the Cape Flattery trailhead, Clallam County

facts.fact: Runs about 12 miles on SR 112 from the eastern edge of the Makah Indian Reservation to Cape Flattery and is the shortest scenic byway in Washington.
The Makah Museum at the Makah Cultural and Research Center shows artifacts 300 to 500 years old from the Ozette archaeological site.

A 1.5-mile round-trip trail leads through forest to the Cape Flattery viewpoint, the northwesternmost point of the contiguous United States, looking out to Tatoosh Island; a Makah Recreation Permit is required for outdoor activities.

byways.review: State tourism now calls it Cape Flattery Scenic Byway. Catalog line is 34 mi against the 12 mi the state gives; it probably includes part of SR 112 east of the reservation (check overlap with the Strait of Juan de Fuca Highway).

byways.name: Cascade Loop Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Washington State Scenic Byway and National Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 2, US 97 Alt, US 97, SR 153, SR 20, SR 525 and the Mukilteo-Clinton ferry, a loop through Snohomish, King, Chelan, Okanogan, Skagit and Island counties

facts.fact: The loop is about 440 miles and was designated a National Scenic Byway in 2021.
It crosses the Cascades through Leavenworth, Wenatchee, Chelan and the Methow Valley, returns through the Skagit Valley and ends on Whidbey Island.
WSDOT closes SR 20 between mileposts 134 and 171 each winter, so the full loop can only be driven from mid-spring to late fall.

byways.review: Catalog labels it 'Regional Scenic Byway'; it has been a National Scenic Byway since 2021. It contains the Stevens Pass Greenway, North Cascades Scenic Highway and Whidbey Scenic Isle Way.

byways.name: Cascade Valleys Heritage Corridor
byways.where: SR 202 from Woodinville (SR 522) to North Bend (I-90), King County

facts.fact: Follows SR 202 for about 30 miles between Woodinville and North Bend through the Sammamish and Snoqualmie valleys.
Woodinville has over 130 wine producers; Snoqualmie has the Northwest Railway Museum and a visitor center about the falls' meaning to the Snoqualmie Tribe.
North Bend and the valley are known as filming locations for the television series Twin Peaks.

byways.review: Older lists call it Cascade Valleys Scenic Byway.

byways.name: Chinook Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Washington State Scenic Byway, All-American Road and National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 410 from Enumclaw over Chinook Pass to Naches, King, Pierce and Yakima counties

facts.fact: Runs about 92 miles on SR 410 from Enumclaw across the northeast corner of Mount Rainier National Park and over Chinook Pass to Naches; designated an All-American Road in 1998.
Federation Forest State Park near Greenwater protects 574 acres of old-growth forest.
Chinook Pass closes from late fall to late spring; Sunrise, reached from the White River entrance, sits at 6,400 feet, the highest point in the park reachable by car.

byways.review: Older state lists use 'Chinook Pass Scenic Byway'.

byways.name: Chuckanut Drive
byways.where: SR 11 from I-5 at Burlington to Bellingham (Fairhaven), Skagit and Whatcom counties

facts.fact: Opened in 1916, Chuckanut Drive is counted among Washington's earliest scenic drives; it began as an 1890s logging road linking the Skagit Valley to Bellingham.
The road crosses Skagit Valley farmland, then winds along the shore with views of the San Juan Islands past Larrabee State Park.
The Samish Flats near the route are a raptor-viewing area in winter.

byways.name: Columbia River Gorge Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 14 from Washougal (Gibbons Creek) east to Maryhill, Clark, Skamania and Klickitat counties

facts.fact: Follows SR 14 along the Washington side of the Columbia River between Camas and Maryhill through the Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area.
The landscape shifts from wet forest in the west to rolling hills and dry country in the east.
Maryhill at the east end has the Maryhill Museum of Art and the Maryhill Stonehenge memorial; Stevenson has the Columbia Gorge Museum.

byways.review: Catalog is ~85 mi; the byway also shares SR 14 with the Lewis and Clark Trail.

byways.name: Coulee Corridor Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Washington State Scenic Byway and National Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 17 and SR 155 (with a short piece of US 2) from Othello through Coulee City and Grand Coulee to Omak, Adams, Grant and Okanogan counties

facts.fact: Runs about 150 miles on SR 17 and SR 155 from Othello to Omak and was designated a National Scenic Byway in 2005.
The route follows channels cut by Ice Age floods and passes Sun Lakes-Dry Falls State Park, Banks Lake (a 27-mile reservoir) and Grand Coulee Dam.
The upper section crosses the Colville Reservation, and the corridor records more than half of the state's 346 annual bird species, including migrating sandhill cranes.

byways.name: Bay-2-Bay Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 105 from Aberdeen through Westport, Grayland and Tokeland to Raymond, Grays Harbor and Pacific counties

facts.fact: Follows SR 105 between Aberdeen and Raymond, about 50 miles, with a short spur to Westport.
Westport has the Grays Harbor Lighthouse; Tokeland has the Shoalwater Bay Heritage Museum of the Shoalwater Bay Indian Tribe.
Cranberry farms and the Cranberry Museum lie along the route.

byways.review: Renamed: the same SR 105 route was the Cranberry Coast Scenic Byway on older WSDOT and Scenic America lists. Catalog line is only ~22 mi of the ~50; check whether the Westport spur and the Tokeland-Raymond stretch are drawn.

byways.name: Hidden Coast Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 109 from Hoquiam along the ocean beaches to Taholah, Grays Harbor County

facts.fact: Follows SR 109 for about 41 miles between Hoquiam and Taholah.
At Copalis Beach the Copalis Ghost Forest of centuries-old stumps stands near the sand; Pacific Beach and Moclips have wide clamming beaches.
Taholah, near the mouth of the Quinault River, is the headquarters of the Quinault Indian Nation and has the Quinault Cultural Center and Museum.

byways.review: Not in the catalog. WSDOT layer row has RouteID 109, Designation 'Scenic Highway'.

byways.name: Lewis and Clark Trail Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 103, SR 100, US 101, SR 401, SR 4, SR 432, I-5, SR 14, I-82, US 395, I-182, US 12 and SR 124 from the Long Beach Peninsula up the Columbia and Snake to Clarkston

facts.fact: About 572 miles from Clarkston on the Idaho line to the Pacific, following the Corps of Discovery along the Snake and Columbia rivers.
Dayton has the Columbia County Courthouse, completed in 1887 and Washington's oldest working courthouse; nearby Patit Creek was a Corps resting place.
Clarkston is a gateway to Hells Canyon and to Nez Perce history.
The western ends are Leadbetter Point State Park (north branch) and Cape Disappointment State Park (south branch).

byways.review: Catalog name is 'Lewis and Clark Trail Highway'. Its catalog line (544 mi) overlaps the Columbia River Gorge byway on SR 14. The separate catalog entry 'U.S. 12 Snake River Bridge to Walla Walla Scenic Byway' is a piece of this route.

byways.name: Mount Baker Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 542 from I-5 in Bellingham through Deming, Maple Falls and Glacier to Artist Point, Whatcom County

facts.fact: Follows SR 542 about 58 miles from Bellingham to Mount Baker, also called the Mount Baker Highway.
Passes the Nooksack River, Nooksack Falls east of Glacier, and old-growth forest; Deming holds an annual logging show.
The last 2.7 miles to Artist Point close east of Glacier from about mid-October or early November until mid to late June.

byways.review: State tourism calls it Mount Baker Highway.

byways.name: Mountains to Sound Greenway
byways.designation: Washington State Scenic Byway and National Scenic Byway
byways.where: I-90 from Seattle/Issaquah over Snoqualmie Pass to Thorp, King and Kittitas counties

facts.fact: Follows I-90 from Puget Sound over Snoqualmie Pass and officially ends at Thorp; designated a National Scenic Byway in 1998.
It lies within the Mountains to Sound Greenway National Heritage Area, which covers 1.5 million acres around I-90.
Issaquah, along the route, has a salmon hatchery and is the gateway to the Issaquah Alps.

byways.review: Ends officially at Thorp; the heritage area extends to Ellensburg.

byways.name: North Cascades Scenic Highway
byways.designation: Washington State Scenic Byway and National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 20 from Sedro-Woolley through Concrete, Newhalem and Washington Pass to Twisp, Skagit, Whatcom and Okanogan counties

facts.fact: Follows SR 20 about 140 miles between Sedro-Woolley and the Methow Valley through the North Cascades National Park Complex.
Diablo Lake is known for its turquoise water, and the Washington Pass Overlook looks across to Liberty Bell Mountain.
Concrete has tall cement silos; WSDOT closes the highway between mileposts 134 and 171 from late November to late April or early May.

byways.review: Part of the Cascade Loop.

byways.name: North Pend Oreille Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 31 from Tiger through Ione and Metaline Falls to the Canadian border, Pend Oreille County

facts.fact: Follows SR 31 about 27 miles from Tiger to the Canadian border and is part of the International Selkirk Loop.
At Tiger the Tiger Historical Center and Museum occupies a 1913 store and post office, the only building left of the town.
Metaline Falls, a former mining town, has the Washington Hotel and Cutter Theater; Gardner Cave at Crawford State Park Heritage Site is one of the state's longest limestone caves.

byways.review: Washington leg of the International Selkirk Loop.

byways.name: Okanogan Trails Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 97 from Pateros through Brewster, Okanogan, Omak, Tonasket and Oroville to the Canadian border, Okanogan County

facts.fact: Follows US 97 about 80 miles between Pateros and the Canadian border, partly along the western edge of the Colville Reservation.
Near Brewster is the site of Fort Okanogan, the first inland American fur trading post.
Omak holds the Omak Stampede and Suicide Race on the second weekend of August; Okanogan's county museum has a replica Old West town.

byways.review: Catalog line ~80 mi matches.

byways.name: Pacific Coast Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 101 from the Astoria-Megler Bridge north through Raymond and Aberdeen, around the Olympic Peninsula by Forks and Port Angeles, and down Hood Canal to Olympia

facts.fact: Follows US 101 about 350 miles from Olympia around Hood Canal and the Olympic Peninsula to Long Beach.
Hood Canal towns such as Hoodsport and Union are known for oysters; Sequim is known for its lavender fields.
Port Angeles is the base for Olympic National Park and has ferry service from Canada.

byways.review: State GIS omits US 101 between Raymond and Queets (Aberdeen-Hoquiam to Queets is not statutory); the byway's named route still uses it.

byways.name: Palouse Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 26, SR 27, SR 194, US 195, SR 271, SR 272 and SR 278 in Whitman County

facts.fact: A network of highways south of Spokane, including US 195, SR 26, SR 27 and SR 272, about 208 miles through rolling hills and farmland with buttes.
Colfax sits just south of Steptoe Butte on the Palouse River; Uniontown's St. Boniface Church, built 1905, is billed as Washington's first consecrated Catholic church.
A detour on SR 261 leads to Palouse Falls, which drops nearly 200 feet into a canyon.

byways.review: The byway is a network of highways, not a single line; Palouse Falls (via SR 261) is a side trip.

byways.name: Pend Oreille Valley Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 20 from Newport north along the Pend Oreille River through Usk and Cusick to Tiger, Pend Oreille County

facts.fact: Runs north from Newport on SR 20 to Tiger, following the Pend Oreille River, which flows north toward Canada.
River pilings still stand from the log-boom holding areas that fed the Diamond Match Company mill at Cusick, which cut western white pine.
Manresa Grotto on the Kalispel Reservation north of Usk, a cave used by early Catholic missionaries, is on the National Register; the Kalispel Tribe keeps a bison herd visible from LeClerc Road.

byways.review: Not on State of Washington Tourism's list or the older Scenic America roster; listed by Scenic WA among the 29. It is the Washington leg of the International Selkirk Loop south of Tiger.

byways.name: San Juan Islands Scenic Byway
byways.where: Washington State Ferries route from Anacortes, with county roads on San Juan Island and Orcas Island, San Juan County

facts.fact: Combines about 30 miles of ferry 'marine highway' from Anacortes with 85 miles of drives on San Juan and Orcas islands.
Roche Harbor on San Juan Island is a historic marina village; Eastsound is Orcas Island's main town near Moran State Park.
Added to the state scenic system by the Legislature in 2009.

byways.review: Island roads are the 'COUNTY ROAD' row (OBJECTID 108) of the WSDOT layer; ferry legs are 'Ferry Route' rows.

byways.name: Sherman Pass Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Washington State Scenic Byway and National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 20 from Republic over Sherman Pass to Kettle Falls, Ferry and Stevens counties

facts.fact: Follows SR 20 about 40 miles between Republic and Kettle Falls.
Sherman Pass, at 5,575 feet, is Washington's highest maintained mountain pass, crossing the Kettle River Range in the Colville National Forest.
Republic has the Stonerose Interpretive Center and Eocene Fossil Site; the route passes a CCC camp site and a log flume heritage site before reaching Lake Roosevelt at Kettle Falls.

byways.review: State tourism page has no byway-organization link; Scenic WA's page is /sherman-pass-crystal-falls-road-trip.

byways.name: Spirit Lake Memorial Highway
byways.designation: Washington State Scenic Byway and National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 504 from I-5 at Castle Rock up the North Fork Toutle River to Johnston Ridge, Cowlitz and Skamania counties

facts.fact: SR 504 is a 52-mile route into the area devastated by the May 18, 1980, eruption of Mount St. Helens, described as the only scenic byway that enters a volcanic blast zone.
Coldwater Lake formed when the 1980 debris avalanche dammed Coldwater Creek; Johnston Ridge Observatory looks into the crater.

SR 504 runs 52 miles along the North Fork Toutle River. The state rebuilt most of the highway from 1988 to 1997 on a new alignment; a May 2023 slide destroyed the Spirit Lake Outlet Bridge at milepost 49 and closed the road east of Coldwater Lake, with rebuilding begun in April 2026.

byways.review: The last few miles to Johnston Ridge have been closed since the May 2023 South Coldwater slide; WSDOT began rebuilding the bridge in April 2026. Not on the State of Washington Tourism list.

byways.name: Stevens Pass Greenway
byways.designation: Washington State Scenic Byway, National Scenic Byway and National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 2 from Monroe over Stevens Pass to Peshastin, Snohomish, King and Chelan counties

facts.fact: Follows US 2 about 90 miles from Monroe to Peshastin through the Skykomish Valley and over Stevens Pass; designated a National Scenic Byway in 2005.
Crosses two national forests, the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie and the Okanogan-Wenatchee.
Passes Wallace Falls State Park and the towns of Sultan, Gold Bar, Index and Skykomish; Leavenworth, east of the pass, is built in a Bavarian style.

byways.review: stevenspassgreenway.org redirects fine over https.

byways.name: Strait of Juan de Fuca Highway
byways.designation: Washington State Scenic Byway and National Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 112 from west of Port Angeles through Joyce, Clallam Bay and Sekiu to Neah Bay, Clallam County

facts.fact: Follows SR 112 about 60 miles from a few miles west of Port Angeles to Neah Bay; designated a National Scenic Byway in 2000.
Joyce has a general store and an annual wild blackberry festival; Salt Creek Recreation Area is known for tidepools at Tongue Point.
The route ends at Neah Bay on the Makah Reservation, where the Makah Museum and the Cape Flattery Scenic Byway begin.

byways.name: Swiftwater Corridor Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 903, SR 970, SR 10 and US 97 from Salmon La Sac through Roslyn and Cle Elum to Thorp and Ellensburg, Kittitas County

facts.fact: Follows SR 903, SR 970, SR 10 and US 97 from the Salmon La Sac campground near Roslyn to Ellensburg.
Roslyn, incorporated in 1889 as a coal town, has a historic district listed on the National Register in 1978.
The Thorp Grist Mill, built in 1883 and run until 1946, keeps handmade wooden milling machinery.

byways.review: Catalog name 'Swift Water Corridor'; catalog line is ~25 mi of ~42 and centered near Cle Elum-Thorp, so the Salmon La Sac (SR 903 / county road) and Thorp-Ellensburg ends may be missing.

byways.name: Whidbey Scenic Isle Way
byways.where: SR 525 and SR 20 from the Clinton ferry landing to Deception Pass, Island County

facts.fact: Follows SR 525 and SR 20 about 48 miles the length of Whidbey Island from Clinton to Deception Pass State Park.
Coupeville, one of Washington's oldest towns, sits on Penn Cove next to Ebey's Landing National Historical Reserve.
The island is reached by the Deception Pass Bridge or by ferry from Mukilteo to Clinton; Oak Harbor has the Pacific Northwest Naval Air Museum.

byways.review: Catalog name 'Whidbey Island Scenic Byway'. Part of the Cascade Loop.

byways.name: White Pass Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Washington State Scenic Byway, National Scenic Byway and National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 12 from I-5 near Napavine/Marys Corner through Mossyrock, Morton, Randle and Packwood over White Pass to Naches, Lewis and Yakima counties

facts.fact: Follows US 12 about 124 miles from Marys Corner near I-5 over White Pass to Naches; designated a National Scenic Byway in 2009.
Mossyrock lies between Mayfield Lake and Riffe Lake; Morton keeps its historic train depot.
Randle has the Cowlitz Valley Ranger District station of the Gifford Pinchot National Forest; Packwood sits on the Cowlitz River near Mount Rainier's Stevens Canyon entrance.

byways.review: Tourism gives 124 mi from Marys Corner; catalog 119 mi.

byways.name: Yakama Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 97 from Union Gap through Toppenish and over Satus Pass to Goldendale and SR 14 near Maryhill, Yakima and Klickitat counties

facts.fact: Runs on US 97 from Union Gap through Toppenish and Goldendale to SR 14 near the Maryhill Museum, much of it across the Yakama Reservation; it is spelled for the Yakama people, not the city of Yakima.
Toppenish lies entirely within the reservation and has 76 historical murals; the Northern Pacific Railway Museum occupies its 1911 depot.
South of the valley the road climbs through the Simcoe Mountains over Satus Pass; Goldendale has a public observatory.

byways.review: Wikipedia's list calls it 'Yakima Scenic Byway' in error. Not on the State of Washington Tourism list.

byways.name: Yakima River Canyon Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 821 from I-82 near Selah up the Yakima River Canyon to Ellensburg, Yakima and Kittitas counties

facts.fact: Follows SR 821 along the Yakima River between Ellensburg and the Yakima Valley through a dry canyon of basalt cliffs.
The Bureau of Land Management runs five recreation sites in the canyon: Umtanum Creek, Lmuma Creek, Big Pines, Bighorn and Roza.
Unlike the state's high passes, the canyon road usually stays open in winter.

byways.review: Not in the catalog. WSDOT layer row RouteID 821.

byways.name: U.S. 12, Snake River Bridge to Walla Walla
byways.designation: Scenic and Recreational Highway segment (part of the Lewis and Clark Trail)
byways.where: US 12 from the Snake River bridge near the Tri-Cities through Wallula and Touchet to Walla Walla, Walla Walla County

facts.fact: RCW 47.39.020 places US 12 from SR 124 near the Tri-Cities east through Wallula and Touchet toward Clarkston in the scenic and recreational highway system.
Walla Walla has more than 100 wineries; the segment is part of the Lewis and Clark Trail Scenic Byway.

byways.review: Not a separately named state byway. Recommend hiding or merging this catalog entry into lewis-and-clark-trail-highway-2234.

byways.name: International Selkirk Loop
byways.where: SR 20 and SR 31 from Newport north to the Canadian border (Washington leg of a 280-mile loop through Idaho and British Columbia)

facts.fact: The International Selkirk Loop is a 280-mile loop through Washington, British Columbia and Idaho, designated an All-American Road in 2005, described as North America's only multi-national scenic loop.
The Washington section follows SR 20 and SR 31 between Newport and the Canadian border and includes the North Pend Oreille Scenic Byway.
Near Usk the Kalispel Tribe of Indians keeps a bison herd visible from LeClerc Road.

byways.review: Its Washington roads are the state's Pend Oreille Valley and North Pend Oreille scenic byways; State of Washington Tourism lists the loop among its byways too.

byways.name: Mountain Loop Scenic Byway
byways.where: Mountain Loop Highway (county road and Forest Road 20) from Granite Falls via Verlot and Barlow Pass to Darrington, Snohomish County

facts.fact: Links Granite Falls and Darrington; first pushed through by miners in 1891, later built up by loggers and the Civilian Conservation Corps, and designated a scenic byway in 1991.
The Verlot Public Service Center was built by the CCC between 1933 and 1942 and is on the National Register of Historic Places.
A 14-mile middle section is single-lane gravel, and snow at Barlow Pass usually limits the full loop to late spring through fall.

byways.review: Older WSDOT/Scenic America rosters counted it among the 29 Washington byways; current state lists do not.

issues: No current WSDOT page lists the named byways. The old wsdot.wa.gov/LocalPrograms/ScenicByways/ pages (archived 2009-2019) redirect to a generic Local Programs page. The member list here combines State of Washington Tourism (25 pages), Scenic WA (a private publisher that lists 29) and Scenic America's 2020 one-pager (29, from the WSDOT roster). The rosters differ: Scenic America has Mountain Loop and Cranberry Coast; Scenic WA has Pend Oreille Valley and Bay-2-Bay instead; tourism leaves out Spirit Lake, Swiftwater, Yakama and Pend Oreille Valley.

Designation is statutory by route segment (RCW 47.39.020 and RCW 47.42.140), not by byway name. The WSDOT layer has no name field. 'Description' (segment limits) is the only text field, and some rows repeat (e.g. SR 105 appears twice, SR 123/SR 706/I-90/US 2/US 97 appear once as 'Scenic Highway' and again as 'Scenic Areas Designated'). Filter on Designation='Scenic Highway' to avoid duplicates. Named byways span several rows, so lines for byways need route+milepost assembly.

Statutory scenic segments that belong to no named byway: SR 3, SR 4, SR 6, SR 7, SR 8, SR 9, SR 19, SR 25, SR 104, SR 106, SR 116, SR 119, SR 122, SR 123, SR 141, SR 142, SR 165, SR 206, SR 211, SR 215, SR 231, SR 261, SR 262, SR 501, SR 503, SR 505, SR 508, SR 547, US 395 Colville to Kettle Falls, SR 202, US 97 Ellensburg to Peshastin, US 97 Alt, I-82 south of the Tri-Cities, the Washington State Ferries routes, plus the I-5 Skagit Valley Agricultural Scenic Corridor (Starbird Rd to Bow Hill Rd). They are left out of the chapter.
Catalog 'Cascade Loop' is labelled Regional Scenic Byway; it became a National Scenic Byway in 2021 (State of Washington Tourism).
Catalog 'Cranberry Coast Scenic Byway' is the route now marketed as Bay-2-Bay Scenic Byway (SR 105, Aberdeen to Raymond, about 50 mi). The catalog line is only ~22 mi.
Catalog 'U.S. 12 Snake River Bridge to Walla Walla Scenic Byway' (65308) is a piece of the Lewis and Clark Trail and not a separately named byway. Suggest merging or hiding it.
Catalog 'Cape Flattery Tribal Scenic Byway' is 34 mi but the byway is 12 mi. It may overlap the Strait of Juan de Fuca Highway on SR 112.
Catalog 'Swift Water Corridor' is ~25 mi of a ~42 mi route and may miss the Salmon La Sac and Ellensburg ends.

Spirit Lake Memorial Highway (SR 504): the road east of Coldwater Lake to Johnston Ridge has been closed since the May 2023 South Coldwater slide. Bridge reconstruction began April 2026 (Wikipedia SR 504). Check status before claiming the observatory is open.
Hidden Coast Scenic Byway (SR 109) and Yakima River Canyon Scenic Byway (SR 821) are not in the catalog. Each has one clean row in the WSDOT layer (gisValue given against the 'Description' field).
stateofwatourism.com byway pages are the most consistent official pages; byway-org URLs were all checked and return 200. stevenspassgreenway.org was linked as http by tourism, and https works.
